segments.he: הַשֵּׁנִי אוֹמֵר: ״אַף אֲנִי כָּמוֹהוּ״. אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, ״אַף אֲנִי כָּמוֹהוּ״ כָּשֵׁר בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וּבְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת, וּמַעֲלָה הוּא דַּעֲבוּד רַבָּנַן. וְהָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר, אוֹקְמוּהָ רַבָּנַן אַדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that after the eldest witness states the exact wording of the curse, «the second» witness does not repeat it, but he «says: I too» heard «as he» did. «Reish Lakish says: Conclude from it» that saying: «I too» heard «as he» did, is «valid» testimony by Torah law, both «in» cases of «monetary law and in» cases of «capital law. And» the requirement that every witness must relate his testimony separately «is a higher standard that the Sages instituted, and here, since it is not possible» to fulfill this requirement, as it is not appropriate for a blasphemous statement to be repeated several times, «the Sages established» the matter «according to Torah law» and did not require that every witness repeat the curse.
